"# Crew compliance shared folder

Working files beside the crew systems. Exports are snapshots taken when they were run; the crew register, roster and duty-actuals databases are the record.

- `ftl-audit-field-guide.md`: the form of the findings, the block close, the notices and the audit request.
- `roster-export-2026-09-21.csv`: last week's roster export.
- `manual/`: printed copies of the operations manual, chapter 7.
- `techlog/`: technical-log pages, named by aircraft, date and page number.
- `duty-control/`: duty control's call log, one entry per file, named by identifier, date and time.

Commander's discretion reports are filed in the discretion-reports database beside the duty actuals.
Generated assets in this folder

- Manual PDFs: typeset with ReportLab (BSD).
- Every name, organisation, aircraft registration and identifier is invented.
# FTL audit: field guide for the September 2026 block

This guide fixes the form of every record the audit writes. The rules come from the operations manual, chapter 7, in the revision that applies to each duty.

## Findings database

One record per exceedance in the findings database for the block. The base assigns the Reference (FTL-nnnnn) when the record is created; do not type one.

- Title: `<staff number> <duty reference or window end date> <limit type>`, separated by single spaces.
- Staff number: the five-digit staff number.
- Duty ref: the duty reference for FDP, DISCRETION and REST findings; for cumulative findings, the last day of the first window that exceeds, as YYYY-MM-DD.
- Limit type: one of FDP, DISCRETION, REST, DUTY_7D, DUTY_14D, DUTY_28D. A duty with more than one exceedance gets one record per limit type; a cumulative limit gets one record per crew member, for the first window that exceeds it.
- Edition: Rev 13 or Rev 14, the revision that applies to the duty, or for a cumulative finding to the window's last day.
- Limit min, Actual min, Excess min: whole minutes as numbers.

=== manual/OM-A-chapter-7-revision-13.pdf
Fernhollow Air Operations Manual Part A, Chapter 7: Flight and Duty Time Limitations

Revision 13. Withdrawn at 00:00 base local time on 15 September 2026 and superseded by Revision
14. Retained for duties that reported before that instant.

7.1 Which revision applies

7.1.1 A revision applies to every duty whose report time, expressed in base local time, falls
on or after the revision's effective instant. The roster day printed on a roster line does not
decide the revision; nor does the date in Coordinated Universal Time.

7.1.2 Base local time for Aberdeen and Edinburgh crews is UTC plus one hour for the whole of
September 2026. The operations records hold times in UTC.

7.2 Definitions

7.2.1 A flight duty period (FDP) runs from the time a crew member reports for duty, including
any positioning that precedes flying, to the on-blocks time at the end of the last sector
flown.

7.2.2 A duty period is an FDP plus 30 minutes of post-flight duty, or a standby period.

7.2.3 A sector is one flight from off-blocks to on-blocks. A diversion and the return flight
are two sectors.

7.2.4 Positioning immediately before a flight duty period is part of that flight duty period.
It does not count as a sector.

7.3 Maximum flight duty period

7.3.1 The maximum FDP is read from Appendix A by the report time in base local time and the
number of sectors.

7.3.2 An FDP longer than the Appendix A maximum is an exceedance unless the commander extended
it under 7.4.

7.4 Commander's discretion

7.4.1 The commander may extend an FDP by up to 02:00 beyond the Appendix A maximum.

7.4.2 An extension stands only if the commander's discretion report for that duty is filed and
signed by the commander. An extension without a filed, signed report is treated as no
extension.

7.4.3 An FDP longer than the Appendix A maximum plus the extension allowed by 7.4.1 is a
discretion exceedance, me

{"description": "Page archived actuals via search", "prompt": "You have MCP tools for a Notion-like service (load schemas with ToolSearch query "select:mcp__LightNotion__login,mcp__LightNotion__search"). Task: dump every "duty actuals" page via the search endpoint to disk. Read-only — never create, update or archive anything.

Steps:
1. Call mcp__LightNotion__login with os_cfg {} to get a session_id.
2. Call mcp__LightNotion__search with query "actuals", page_size 100, and start_cursor omitted, then "100", "200", ... continuing while has_more is true (expect roughly 7,600 matches, so up to ~cursor 7600). Make calls ONE AT A TIME (sequentially). If you get "429 Too Many Requests ... retry after N seconds", retry the same cursor (if foreground sleep is blocked in Bash, just retry). Each big result is auto-saved to a file under the session's tool-results directory (the error message gives the path); do not read file contents into your context. If a page comes back inline because it is small (the last page), re-request it with a start_cursor 100 below the total so it is a full page and is saved to file instead; overlapping is fine.
3. With Bash + python3 (no jq), load every saved search result file you produced (JSON: {"status","output":{"results":[...],"next_cursor","has_more"}}), keep results whose "parent_id" is "db-duty-actuals-to-0914" or "db-duty-actuals-from-0915", dedupe by "id", and write them as a JSON list to /workspace/work/actuals_search.json.

Report back only: number of unique rows per parent_id, the final cursor reached and whether has_more became false, and any cursors that failed or any sign that results were capped/truncated (e.g. has_more false well before ~7,600 or a note in the response).", "subagent_type": "general-purpose", "model": "sonnet"}

import json
from datetime import datetime,timedelta
INS=set('45175 44049 32894 47639 35947 36330 49130 37712 39638 32200 48146 49580 36107 31279 45269 37488 32319 49946 43699 38571 45677 40672 31527 31564 44873 43840 49301 45172'.split())

def T(s): return datetime.strptime(s,'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ') if s else None
A=[x for x in json.load(open('/workspace/work/actuals_search.json')) if P(x,'Staff number') in INS]

TL=json.load(open('/workspace/work/tl.json'))
EOF
python3 -c "
from load import *
from collections import Counter
print(len(A),Counter(P(x,'Type') for x in A))
print(Counter(P(x,'Duty ref').split('-')[0] for x in A))
print('no roster',[x['title'] for x in A if (P(x,'Duty ref'),P(x,'Staff number')) not in RO])
ak={(P(x,'Duty ref'),P(x,'Staff number')) for x in A}

# techlog matching by aircraft & flights
fd=[x for x in A if P(x,'Type')=='Flight duty']
used=set()
for x in fd:
  fl=P(x,'Flights').split(); ac=P(x,'Aircraft'); rep=T(P(x,'Report (UTC)'))
  for k,v in TL.items():

    d=datetime.strptime(v['date'],'%Y-%m-%d')
    if abs((d-rep.replace(hour=0,minute=0)).days)>1: continue
    tf=[s[1] for s in v['secs']]
    if set(tf)&set(fl):
      used.add(k)

"
